REPORT HIGHLIGHTS / FACT SHEET Office of the Suffolk County Comptroller | 1 Objectives To determine which subrecipients of federal funding that passed through Suffolk County were required to have a Single Audit, determine compliance of the Single Audit reports with the requirements of OMB Uniform Guidance, and determine if any of the S ingle Audit reports reviewed contained findings that relate to programs that received federal funding that passed through Suffolk County.

APPENDIX A: SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY Office of the Suffolk County Comptroller | 13 The Suffolk County Comptroller’s Office conducted a review of the federal funding that Suffolk County passed through to subrecipients for the period January 1, 202 4 through December 31, 2024.

Subrecipients that expend less than $750,000 of federal financial assistance in their fiscal year are exempt from the Single Audit; however, they must submit an exemption letter to the Comptroller’s Office with a Schedule of Federal Funds Expended. Federal agencies and profit- making entities may be subrecipients; however, they are not required to procure a Single Audit and are exempt from subrecipient monitoring. In order to accomplish our objectives, we performed the following procedures: • Obtained and summarized information regarding the amount of federal funding passed through to subrecipients from all Departments. • Informed County Departments that they are responsible for subrecipient monitoring, which includes obtaining a copy of the subrecipient’s Single Audit report or a Single Audit exemption letter 3 and a Schedule of Federal Funds Expended. • Reviewed the Advisories, sections of the OMB Uniform Guidance pertaining to subrecipient monitoring, and the OMB Compliance Supplement applicable to t

• Performed a desk review of the subrecipient’s Single Audit report and determined compliance with OMB Uniform Guidance. Additionally, notify the department(s) of subrecipient findings related to the department’s pass -through funding. • Notified the subrecipients of any deficiencies in their Single Audit reports and requested corrective action.
